extracted.intended_audience: Catholic catechism students / general faithful (lay readers, children, catechumens)
extracted.subtask_description: A catechetical exposition of the Church's marks, the nature and effects of the seven Sacraments, and detailed rules and rites for Baptism (including who may administer it, how it is performed, and its theological effects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marks of the true Church (One, Holy, Catholic, Apostolic)
rubrics_metrics.description: The true Church of Christ possesses all the marks: it is one, holy, catholic (universal), and apostolic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catholic means it 'subsists in all ages, teaches all nations, and maintains all truth.' Apostolic means founded by Christ on His Apostles and governed by their lawful successors and never ceasing to teach their doctrine. The Church must be visible so men may see and know it; absence of these marks indicates a church is not the true Church of Christ. The Holy Ghost preserves the Church's undying life and infallible authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three necessary elements of a Sacrament
rubrics_metrics.description: To constitute a Sacrament there must be (1) an outward (visible) sign, (2) institution by Our Lord, and (3) the power to give grace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Baptism's outward sign is pouring water and words; Confirmation's outward sign is anointing with oil, bishop's prayer, and laying on of hands; Penance's outward sign is the priest's words of absolution. 'Institution by Christ' is necessary so the Church cannot make new sacraments or abolish old ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of the seven Sacraments
rubrics_metrics.description: There are seven Sacraments: Baptism, Confirmation, Holy Eucharist, Penance, Extreme Unction, Holy Orders, and Matrimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sacraments are presented as covering the spiritual life analogous to bodily life: birth (Baptism), strengthening (Confirmation), feeding (Eucharist), cure (Penance), help at death (Extreme Unction), governance (Holy Orders), and family life (Matrimony).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of sacramental power
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sacraments have the power of giving grace from the merits of Jesus Christ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Our Lord merited grace by His death and appointed the Sacraments as the chief means by which grace is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: sacraments that give sanctifying grace vs. those that increase it
rubrics_metrics.description: Some sacraments (Baptism and Penance) give sanctifying grace when it is not present; others (Confirmation, Eucharist, Extreme Unction, Holy Orders, Matrimony) increase sanctifying grace in souls already in a state of grace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baptism and Penance are called 'Sacraments of the dead' because they take away sin (the death of the soul) and give life; the others are 'Sacraments of the living' because they presuppose and augment existing grace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sacrilege and unworthy reception
rubrics_metrics.description: Receiving Sacraments of the living while in mortal sin is sacrilege; sacrilege also includes willful disrespect or abuse of sacred persons, places, or things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of sacrilege: using sacred vessels for common use, stealing from the church, turning the church into a market, or willfully killing/wounding consecrated persons. Unworthy reception (in mortal sin) is a 'great sin' because it abuses a sacred thing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sacramental grace defined
rubrics_metrics.description: Sacramental grace is a special help from God to attain the end for which He instituted each Sacrament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Penance's sacramental grace helps overcome temptation and avoid habitual sins; Confirmation's sacramental grace strengthens one to profess faith or resist doubt. The sacraments both sanctify and help prevent relapse into former sin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of right dispositions for sacraments to give grace
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sacraments always give grace if received with the right dispositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right dispositions examples: in Penance—confessing all mortal sins, true contrition, firm purpose of amendment; in the Eucharist—being in a state of grace and fasting one hour (except in sickness). If dispositions are lacking, sacramental effect may not be received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeatability of sacraments and character-imprinting sacraments
rubrics_metrics.description: Sacraments may be received more than once except Baptism, Confirmation, and Holy Orders, which imprint a spiritual character and therefore are given only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If doubt exists about the validity of a first Baptism, conditional Baptism may be administered (e.g., 'If you are not baptized already, I baptize you now'). The character is a permanent spiritual mark visible after death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning and permanence of the sacramental character
rubrics_metrics.description: The character imprinted by Baptism, Confirmation, and Holy Orders is a spiritual mark which remains forever, even after death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This character shows that the person received those sacraments; if in Heaven it will shine to their honor; if in Hell it will be evidence of their abuse of God's gifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Baptism and its effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Baptism is a Sacrament which cleanses from Original Sin, makes the person a Christian, a child of God, and an heir of Heaven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being 'Christian' means member of the Church; 'child of God' means adopted by grace; 'heir of Heaven' likened to inheritance from Christ's death. Baptism washes away Original Sin and makes one free from its guilt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baptism remits actual sins and temporal punishments if validly received
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual sins and all temporal punishment due to them are remitted by Baptism, provided the person baptized is guilty of any and the baptism is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a mature person is baptized after committing sins of reason, Baptism forgives them so they need not confess them, but one must be truly sorry and intend amendment. Baptism removes both eternal and temporal debt; a person baptized and dying immediately would go to Heaven, not Purgatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of Baptism for salvation
rubrics_metrics.description: Baptism is necessary to salvation because without it one cannot enter the kingdom of Heaven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those who die without Baptism through no fault of their own cannot enter Heaven but will not go to Hell either; they will be in a state of natural peace without seeing God. The text emphasizes the gravity of depriving someone of Baptism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may administer Baptism
rubrics_metrics.description: The priest is the ordinary minister of Baptism (and bishops and the Pope possess this power); in case of necessity anyone with the use of reason may baptize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Ordinary' means the usual minister. 'Necessity' means when the ordinary cannot be had and Baptism is required (e.g., imminent danger of death). Even non-Catholics may validly baptize in necessity if they know the form and intend to do what the Church does. One cannot baptize against the person's will; infants whose parents refuse may be baptized if dying.

rubrics_metrics.name: How Baptism is validly administered (form and matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Baptism is given by pouring water on the head of the person and saying while pouring: 'I baptize thee in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In church solemn Baptism uses consecrated water mixed with holy oil and many ceremonies (salt, spittle, anointings, stole, white garment, candle); in private or necessity plain clean water suffices and the simple form is used. Symbolic meanings explained: salt for wisdom, spittle recalling Christ, stole for Church protection, white garment for purity, candle for light of faith. Private baptisms should later be brought to church for the rest of the ceremonies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of Baptism: water, desire, and blood
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three kinds of Baptism: Baptism of water (the ordinary rite), Baptism of desire, and Baptism of blood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baptism of desire is an ardent wish to receive Baptism and to do all God has ordained for salvation—applies when one has no opportunity for water baptism. Example analogy: perfect contrition saving when no priest present. Baptism of desire is effective where no water or minister is available or when ignorance prevents proper administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for conditional administration of Sacraments
rubrics_metrics.description: Sacraments may be given conditionally when there is doubt whether they were validly given previously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: conditional baptism formula 'If you are not baptized already, I baptize you now.' Converts are often conditionally baptized when validity of prior baptism is uncertain.
